title: netwatch daemon flow log, netwatch.flow.v0
description: One line of the flow log that netwatch daemon --flow-log writes. This validates a line, not a file. Each daily file starts with the header; stdout starts with it once. Every later line is an event: open and close from polling the connection table, connect from the eBPF probes when they loaded, dns from DNS exchanges seen in capture, and dropped. Experimental: this format is outside the 1.0 compatibility promise and can change in any release. Ignore fields you do not know.

header.description: The first line of a file, and of stdout.

sources.description: What this session's events come from.

poll.description: open and close events from polling the connection table. Always true.

ebpf.description: active: the connect probes loaded, so connect events follow and ownerless flows can take their owner. unavailable: they did not; ebpf_error says why. Open set.

ebpf_error.description: Why the probes did not load. Free text.

metadata.description: Names this output's schema, at the same path as every other netwatch output.

netwatch_version.description: The netwatch that wrote this file.

timestamp.description: UTC, RFC 3339 with milliseconds and a Z suffix.

flow.description: A connection that appeared in the polled connection table (open), or reached a closing TCP state, left the table, or was still open when the daemon stopped (close). Metadata only, never payload. A connection shorter than one poll interval is never seen.

ts.description: The poll that saw the event, not the moment of connect() or close().

proto.description: Transport, as the connection table names it. Open set.

process.description: The owning process's name, the latest one known. Null when attribution found no owner.

pid.description: The owning process's id. Null when unknown.

attribution.description: How the owner was matched. ebpf: polling found no owner, and one process alone connected to this destination within five seconds, per the connect probes; a verified owner on a later poll replaces it. Open set.

local.description: Local address and port, as the connection table prints it.

remote.description: Remote address and port, as the connection table prints it.

state.description: TCP state at the event, as the platform names it; empty or a platform word for UDP. Free text.

reason.description: close only. closed: the socket reached a closing TCP state, possibly at the poll that first saw it, so a flow shorter than a poll still gets an open and a close. gone: it left the table with no closing state seen. shutdown: the daemon stopped while it was open. Closed set.

duration_ms.description: close only. From the poll that opened it to the poll that closed it.

host.description: The destination's name from a TLS or QUIC SNI, or a cleartext HTTP Host. Needs packet capture. Absent when none was read.

host_source.description: Where host came from. Open set.

ech.description: Present only when the ClientHello carried Encrypted ClientHello: host is then the outer, public name, not the one the client asked for.

dns_name.description: The name a DNS answer seen in capture gave this address: the name the client asked, not a CNAME target. Absent when no answer for it was seen, or it expired.

rdns.description: Reverse-DNS name of the remote address, when resolved while the flow was open.

asn_org.description: Organisation of the remote address from the ASN database. Absent with no database.

country.description: ISO country code of the remote address from the GeoIP database. Absent with no database.

app_protocol.description: Application protocol the packet decoder recognised. Open set.

bytes_out.description: close only. Approximate, from per-tick rates. Zero without packet capture, which does not mean no traffic.

bytes_in.description: close only. Approximate, from per-tick rates. Zero without packet capture, which does not mean no traffic.

retransmits.description: close only. TCP retransmits seen on the flow; zero without capture.

observed_by.description: How the event was observed. poll: a connection-table poll. Open set.

dropped.description: Events the writer could not keep up with, written as soon as it caught up.

count.description: Events lost since the previous line.

connect.description: One connect() of a TCP or connected UDP socket, as the eBPF probes saw it at connect entry: the moment, the process and the destination. Seen even when the connection is shorter than a poll. Written a tick or two later, joined to the captured stream it started when there is one: that gives local and, from the ClientHello, host. A refused or failed connect is still a connect.

ts.description: When netwatch read the event, within milliseconds of the connect().

process.description: The task's comm: the process name, cut to 15 characters.

pid.description: The process id (thread-group id) that called connect().

local.description: The client side of the captured stream this connect started: the source address and port. Absent without capture, or when no stream matched.

remote.description: Destination address and port, IPv6 in brackets.

host.description: The TLS or QUIC SNI, or HTTP Host, of the matched stream. Absent when there was none to read in time.

host_source.description: Where host came from. Open set.

ech.description: Present only when the ClientHello carried Encrypted ClientHello: host is then the outer, public name, not the one the client asked for.

app_protocol.description: What the decoder made of the matched stream. Open set.

dns_name.description: The name a DNS answer seen in capture gave this address: the name the client asked, not a CNAME target. Absent when no answer for it was seen, or it expired.

dns.description: One DNS exchange over UDP port 53 seen in capture: the query and, when it came, the response, paired by client, server and transaction id. A response for a query capture did not see is written on its own. Encrypted DNS (DoT, DoH) and exchanges on interfaces capture does not see are absent.

ts.description: The query packet's capture time, or the response's when no query was seen.

process.description: Who owns the client socket: from the connection table when it verified one, else from the socket's connect line. Null when neither knew.

attribution.description: How the owner was matched. Absent with a null process. Open set.

qtype.description: The query type by name, or TYPE<n>. Open set.

rcode.description: The response code by name, RCODE<n> for others, or timeout when no response came within three ticks. Open set.

latency_ms.description: From query to response, by capture time, to a tenth of a millisecond. Absent without both.

answers.description: The A and AAAA addresses in the answer section, in order.

cnames.description: The CNAME targets in the answer section, in order.

query_seen.description: Present only when the response came for a query capture did not see.
